messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Proble installing rstah under Sage's R
parts:
On Wednesday, July 23, 2014 11:27:26 PM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:

It looks like this error is the one built with cpp optimization level 0 with g++, see here
https://travis-ci.org/stan-dev/rstan/builds/30479408

Good catch! Indeed, Sage is for some reason building R without any optimization when it has -O2 by default. It is a bit disturbing that we can't build rstan without optimization (which would be useful for debugging at some point), but it is more disturbing that Sage would turn off optimization by default when building R.

Ben

A couple more datapoints :
1) Sages'R indeed needs -O2 (or -O3, but I'd settle for -O2 since -O3 leads to invalid objects for other libraries, such as nloptr, which is the workhorse of a lot of other packages...).

2) I did not (yet) found a way to pass it from R to an installation od rstan othar than via "./RMakevars". GCC mysteries...

I suspect there is something suboptimal in the Sage build. A plain ./configure on the r-devel tree results in

R is now configured for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

So, someone would have to do something other than a plain ./configure to remove the -O2.
3) System's R does not seem to *need* -O2|3, but gives a couple of warnings about 'exceeded limits. Retrying without limits".
I get those also with g++, and I think they are harmless because it succeeds on the retry. They do not appear with clang++.
4) GCC mysteries : any compilation of rstan seem to need about 2 Gb (!!!) of memory. Parallelizing it seriously accelerates the process, but needs as much as 11,2 Gb (!!!!) of RAM.

Not a mystery or at least this is something we have known to be the case for 3 years. With clang++, it is much better in terms of RAM usage. With g++-4.9, you can add the flags -flto and -ffat-lto-objects (see https://gcc.gnu.org/gcc-4.9/changes.html) to CXXFLAGS in ~/.R/Makevars and it is a lot better but not quite as good as clang++.
5) Consequences of 4) : any model compilation (even a small one) on a 2 Gb machine leads to swapping.

I would install clang++ from the Debian repositories and set CC=clang and CXX=clang++ in ~/.R/Makevars

[...]

Yes, so there is some chance that it will break other packages, and I would understand if CRAN makes us get rid of set_cppo() if / when we retry to upload it to CRAN. But set_cppo() in rstan 2.3.0 should have produced a valid ~/.R/Makevars for installing rstan. It is just we can't ensure that ~/.R/Makevars is valid on every user's machine so install_rstan() ignores it in favor of whatever settings R was built with (which are amenable to installing rstan for any binary install of R or a sane source install of R but apparently not Sage's).

Shouldn't setting this option be *internal* to rstan's wrapper functions ? Again, the idea is to avoid to modify the state of thge user's computer. To your garden-variety biostatistician, GCC is something like an endemic disease (fortunately non-mortal (usually...)) ; the CXXFLAGS some sort of prognostic factor. The Stan USER should NOT have to worry with such technical details -but these should be documented for the special cases).

I don't think there is a way to pass a particular set of flags when internally calling stan_model() (to compile the program) that wouldn't get superseded by what is in ~/.R/Makevars because the compilation is actually done with a separate R process. For most users that do not want to worry about such technical details, calling set_cppo() once solves that problem, but it is somewhat evil to the extent it breaks other R packages.
 
 [...]

so that it is correctly formatted and by default uses -O3 because that makes Stan programs run slightly faster than -O2 and much faster than any other optimization level. Setting -O3 probably breaks some other R packages, which I would be sympathetic to if that happened on your system,

It did. More than once ...

but it changes a  non-executable file, is documented and also prints a message to the console when it is called.

Not during installation !

+   install.packages(c("inline", "BH", "RcppEigen"))
+   install.packages("Rcpp", type = "source")

No : here, you unconditionally install whatever Rcpp and BH version happens to be available on CRAN at install time. You should install use the "Depends" field of the DESCRIPTION file, which would install the packages *if necessary* (even with version constraints if necessary).

No:

http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Package-Dependencies

"Field ‘Depends’ should nowadays be used rarely, only for packages which are intended to be put on the search path to make their facilities available to the end user (and not to the package itself)"

and later on in that same section

A package that wishes to make use of header files in other packages needs to declare them as a comma-separated list in the field ‘LinkingTo’ in the DESCRIPTION file. For example 

LinkingTo: link1, link2

As from R 3.0.2 the ‘LinkingTo’ field can have a version requirement which is checked at installation. (In earlier versions of R it would cause the specification to be ignored.)

Specifying a package in ‘LinkingTo’ suffices if these are C++ headers containing source code or static linking is done at installation: the packages do not need to be (and usually should not be) listed in the ‘Depends’ or ‘Imports’ fields. This includes CRAN packages BH and almost all users of RcppArmadillo and RcppEigen.

which is exactly what the DESCRIPTION file in rstan does

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/rstan/develop/rstan/rstan/DESCRIPTION

Depends: R (>= 3.0.2), Rcpp (>= 0.9.10), utils, inline, methods
LinkingTo: Rcpp, RcppEigen, BH (>= 1.54)
Suggests: RUnit, RcppEigen, BH (>= 1.54), parallel

with the added Suggests line to work around the undocumented fact that the rstan vignette would not build without it.

Okay. So why unconditionally install BH and RcppEigen ?

Because BH and RcppEigen are not only needed when the package is built / installed but also when stan_model() is called to compile the user's program. So, you could install rstan but not use it unless BH and RcppEigen are on the disk. CRAN's DESCRIPTION file does not have an idiom for this case. (Re)Installing them unconditionally isn't harmful but wastes a little bandwidth if they are already installed. I suppose I could write some logic to check whether they are installed and what version they have, but I haven't gotten around to it.
